correctness.rationale: The chain polytope is the free join of orthogonal unit cubes, with volume product(m_i!)/n!. Its facets are all L_{a,i}:x_{a,i}=0 and U_sigma:sum x_{a,sigma_a}=1, giving area budgets nr and n sqrt r. Inspected the proof and both actual ridge/codimension metric scripts. An L–L facet pair always defines a ridge, L–U precisely if the zero coordinate is not on selected chain, and U–U precisely if chains change exactly one block; additional crossed equalities exclude other pairs. Coarea factorial/normal Gram calculations give normalized total ridge measures relative to n(n-1)volume: LL=r^2/2, LU=r sqrt r, UU=r sqrt(2r-1)/2; exterior normal angles are pi/2,pi/2,arccos((r-1)/r). Ridge Steiner weighting angle/(2pi) yields the displayed V_{n-2}/volume formula. Independently computed convex hull volume and facet areas for (2,2,2): volume 1/90, boundary/volume 28.3923048454 = 6(3+sqrt3). All-r rank- and profile-independence rests on beta/coarea proof, not finite profiles.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Chain-order result covers the surface term for all m_i>=1 and r, but stops at t^1 and does not cover the t^2/second Steiner formula. Enriched chain theorem gives t^2 for the sign-symmetric body sum ||x^i||infty<=1, not the positive chain polytope; the two shapes differ even after simple scaling.

originality.rationale: Best-knowledge PASS for second Steiner coefficient and the full metric ridge census in canonical unweighted chain polytopes, but the first surface ratio is ALREADY known: the 2026/11/17 published chain-order-interpolation result gives endpoint n(r+sqrt r). The 2026/11/17 exact order-polytope Steiner theorem uses a different nonisometric Euclidean polytope and a different coefficient; enriched chain polytope is a signed free join with different curvature formula. Ahmad–Fourier–Joswig provide facet/face combinatorics, not weighted metric ridge sums. The second coefficient is the substantive independent contribution, while concurrent prior dates and uncatalogued metric formulas are residual risks.
residual_risks: Prior same-day chain-order interpolation already yields the surface component; novelty cannot be attributed to this first coefficient or to general f-vector monotonicity.
No claim for singleton layers in the second-coefficient formula, weighted metrics, arbitrary posets or higher intrinsic volumes; an unindexed t^2 formula remains a historical-priority risk.
